scope: Selected decision review for the bounded features in features.json. Historical decisions are interpreted against current code and current assertions; no ADR is certified wholesale.

decisions.subject: Pattern tiling evaluation and group shape/opacity
decisions.current_reading: The implementation retains cell-level transparency evaluation and applies the painting mark's constants to the evaluated tiling as a whole where a group is needed. The named tests distinguish alpha-on-final-pattern from alpha-per-cell-object and exercise a cell taking its enclosing backdrop.
decisions.assessment: Still relevant and supported for these sampled consumers. The NOTE recommending a single group for raster tiling was not treated as a mandatory optimization independent of visual behavior. Pattern_forms_current owns geometry/anchor gaps.

decisions.subject: DeviceCMYK press as a group blending space
decisions.current_reading: §11.7.2 requires ICCBased CMYK group redefinition and late conversion; current process run selection, `Press` and `Compositing` paths provide a four-component group in the cases asserted.
decisions.assessment: Current fixtures establish selected cases with group-local values and distinct press controls. No unbounded claims about every ICC profile route or press budget are derived from this decision.

decisions.subject: Optional opaque-overprint compatibility blend
decisions.current_reading: §11.7.4.3 says a processor may consider implementing the special mode. This tree does implement it in supported 4-component target contexts. That implementation decision is permitted; once selected, its stated condition and mode arithmetic are conditional shall obligations.
decisions.assessment: Decision remains valid. A device with native three-component additive color space may ignore opaque overprint under §8.6.7, but this does not erase the separate group-space condition in §11.7.4.3. Current test pair has an RGB/no-op case and a four-component page-group discriminating case.

decisions.subject: Cost of overprint support
decisions.current_reading: Implementation cost remains a performance decision, not a normative reading. Current measured route complexity and model-level report distinguish supported semantics from backend capabilities.
decisions.assessment: No current source contradiction found in this shard; performance cost itself was not independently remeasured.

decisions.subject: Separation/DeviceN reversion and special overprint eligibility
decisions.current_reading: §11.7.4.3 Note 2 says a space reverting to an alternate is treated as that alternate when identifying the current space; the §8.6.7 example equates relevant DeviceN and DeviceCMYK paint. `cmyk_tints` and the press-profile test exercise this.
decisions.assessment: Current reading is corroborated by effective text and test name; no new counterexample found. DeviceN NChannel's output-specific spot-plane routing remains under special-colour/press ownership.

decisions.subject: Transfer-function per-component opacity under overprint
decisions.current_reading: §11.7.5.2 explicitly says the overprint result must be source color for that component to qualify as opaque. The paired OPM1 vs OPM0 raster checks paint a non-identity transfer only when the source replaces the component.
decisions.assessment: Strong targeted evidence for the selected case. It does not prove the complete six-condition truth table.

decisions.subject: Spot plane output and simulation availability
decisions.current_reading: §11.7.3 permits keeping spot components independently or substituting alternates. Current code and tests exercise spot-plane output and the RGB alternate route separately; soft-mask groups always lack spot planes and tests compare against alternate-space controls.
decisions.assessment: Consistent in sampled paths. Neither decision implies that an ordinary RGB display can reproduce physical ink appearance.

nonclaims: No general endorsement of all historical ADRs cited by the ledger.
No claim that tests listed in a ledger row establish every source bullet, backend, object type or exact interaction.
No claim of mandatory special overprint mode: the mode is permitted, not required by §11.7.4.3.
No claim that halftone screens must be rasterized on continuous-tone targets.
No inference that producer constraints create reader rejection duties.
